name: Cisco ASA — VPN Credential Brute Force
xql_query:
dataset = cisco_asa_raw
| filter _raw_log contains "109006"
| alter src_ip    = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "from (\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)/"), 0),
        raw_user  = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "for user '(.+?)' from "), 0)
| alter user_name = arrayindex(regextract(raw_user, "([A-Za-z0-9._@'-]+)$"), 0)
| filter src_ip != null
| bin _time span = 30m
| comp count() as fails,
       values(user_name) as users,
       count_distinct(user_name) as targeted_users
       by src_ip, _time
| filter fails >= 10
| fields src_ip, users, fails, targeted_users
description: Many 109006 auth failures from a single IP against the VPN gateway.
alert_name: Cisco ASA — VPN Credential Brute Force
alert_description:
What fired: Many 109006 auth failures from a single IP against the VPN gateway.

Why it matters: an actor is attempting to obtain or brute-force credentials. Assessed severity: High.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1110 - Brute Force (TA0006 - Credential Access); T1110.003 - Password Spraying (TA0006 - Credential Access).

Investigate:
  - Identify the targeted account(s) and the source IP, and check for a SUCCESSFUL authentication following the failures.
  - Determine whether the source is expected; look for MFA prompts, password resets, or new sessions from the same source.
  - Pivot on the alert's key entity (xdm.source.ipv4) to related activity in the same window.
  - Confirm the activity is not expected/authorized for the involved entity before escalating.
